title: Odoo Development
tagline: Build your first Odoo modules: development setup, addon scaffolding, the manifest, models and fields, menus and views, and a service-billing business case.
description: For developers who know Python and want to customize Odoo. You will start with Odoo’s architecture and set up and configure a local development environment.

Step by step, you will scaffold a custom module, write its manifest, add a model and connect it to menus and views, then go deeper into field types and how models are represented and ordered. Guided readings cover form, list, kanban and search views and actions, and the course ends with a business case: designing an automated service-billing and contract-management addon.
learningOutcomes: Explain Odoo’s architecture and where a module fits
Install and configure Odoo for local development
Scaffold a custom addon and write its manifest
Create models with the right field types, representation and ordering
Build menus, actions and form, list, kanban and search views
Plan a custom addon from a business case
whoItsFor: Python developers applying their skills within a business-focused ERP framework
Technical learners specializing in Odoo architecture, modules and customization
ERP technical support staff moving from troubleshooting into structured development
Developers preparing for their first custom-module assignments
requirements: Working knowledge of Python, including functions and classes
Comfort with a code editor and the command line

faq.question: How is this different from Python Fundamentals?
faq.answer: Python Fundamentals teaches the Python language itself. This course applies Python inside the Odoo framework to build modules.

faq.question: Do I need advanced Python?
faq.answer: No, but you should be comfortable with Python basics, including functions and classes. Python Fundamentals covers everything you need.

faq.question: Will I build a module?
faq.answer: Yes. You build a first addon step by step, with a manifest, a model, menus and views.

faq.question: Are integrations or APIs covered?
faq.answer: No. This course focuses on module structure, models, fields and views.
